title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Eight Typical Cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Releases Eight Typical Cases

I. Yuan Qiao'e — Crime of Refusing to Pay Labor Remuneration

(1) Basic Facts

The defendant Yuan Qiao'e was the person in charge of Yunhe County Huaxia Craft Factory (a sole proprietorship) in Zhejiang Province, and jointly operated the factory with her husband Xia Genfa (separately prosecuted). From the beginning of 2011, the factory had been in arrears in paying workers' wages for a long time. In early September 2011, Yuan Qiao'e and Xia Genfa suddenly absconded, and their mobile phones were switched off and could not be reached. On September 9, Yunhe County Bureau of Personnel and Labor Security issued a directive order, instructing Huaxia Craft Factory to pay the overdue workers' wages before September 13. On the same day, Yunhe County People's Court preserved the machinery and equipment of Huaxia Craft Factory by property preservation. On September 21, because Yuan Qiao'e and Xia Genfa failed to perform as scheduled, Yunhe County People's Court formally opened a case for investigation. On October 8, Yuan Qiao'e went to Yunhe County People's Court to verify the overdue workers' wages. By court judgment and mediation, Huaxia Craft Factory owed a total of RMB 290,270.52 in workers' wages. In late October, Yuan Qiao'e absconded again and changed her contact information. On January 15, 2012, the case was transferred to Yunhe County Public Security Bureau, and was filed as a criminal case the next day. On January 19, Yuan Qiao'e voluntarily surrendered to Yunhe County Public Security Bureau and truthfully confessed the main criminal facts.

(2) Judgment

Yunhe County People's Court of Zhejiang Province held after trial that the defendant Yuan Qiao'e, by means of absconding and changing contact information, evaded paying the workers' labor remuneration of over 290,000 yuan, a relatively large amount, and failed to pay after being ordered by the relevant government department; her conduct constituted the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration. Yuan Qiao'e voluntarily surrendered after the incident and truthfully confessed her criminal facts, which constituted voluntary surrender, and a lighter punishment may be imposed according to law. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the defendant Yuan Qiao'e was found guilty of the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration and sentenced to one year imprisonment and a fine of RMB 20,000. After the judgment was announced, Yuan Qiao'e accepted the judgment and did not appeal.

(3) Significance

The Amendment (VIII) to the Criminal Law of the PRC, which came into effect on May 1, 2011, criminalized malicious wage arrears, thereby significantly improving the protection system for workers' rights. Through the strong intervention of criminal law, malicious wage arrears are targeted, unscrupulous employers are deterred, and the legitimate rights and interests of vast numbers of workers are protected from infringement. In this case, the defendant Yuan Qiao'e evaded paying workers' labor remuneration of over 290,000 yuan by absconding, and failed to pay even after being ordered by Yunhe County Bureau of Personnel and Labor Security; she then absconded again and changed her contact information; her conduct constituted the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration. The trial of this case clarified the elements of the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration. The subjective element of this crime should be the purpose of evading payment of workers' labor remuneration; the objective element is the evasion of payment of workers' labor remuneration by means such as transferring property or absconding, or having the ability to pay but failing to pay workers' labor remuneration, with the overdue amount being relatively large, and the precondition being failure to pay after being ordered by the relevant government department. The aim is to strengthen the protection of workers' legitimate rights and interests while also avoiding excessive intervention by criminal law, helping to maintain a healthy and orderly market economy and promoting social harmony and stability.

II. Fu Dehong — Crime of Refusing to Pay Labor Remuneration

(1) Basic Facts

In July 2009, the defendant Fu Dehong operated a garment factory in Huzhou City, Zhejiang Province. On November 19, 2011, due to poor management, in order to evade usury and payment of workers' wages, Fu Dehong absconded with over 10,000 yuan to Hefei City, Anhui Province, Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province, and other places to hide, refusing to pay a total of over 110,000 yuan in workers' wages. Later, despite being ordered by Huzhou Wuxing District Human Resources and Social Security Bureau to pay, he still failed to pay. On July 27, 2012, Fu Dehong was arrested in Zhuzhou City, Hunan Province.

(2) Judgment

Wuxing District People's Court of Huzhou, Zhejiang Province held after trial that the defendant Fu Dehong evaded paying workers' wages by absconding, the amount was relatively large, and he failed to pay after being ordered by the relevant government department; his conduct constituted the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration. Fu Dehong, after being brought to justice, could truthfully confess the criminal facts, and pleaded guilty in court, so a lighter punishment may be imposed according to law. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the defendant Fu Dehong was found guilty of the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration and sentenced to one year and six months imprisonment and a fine of RMB 30,000. After the judgment was announced, Fu Dehong did not appeal, and the judgment has taken effect.

(3) Significance

The issue of malicious wage arrears is a problem that has gradually emerged and become prominent during China's economic and social development in recent years. Against the backdrop of increasingly frequent population mobility and high concentration of labor, this issue concerns the vital interests and basic rights protection of the vast laboring masses, the sense of life stability and well-being of the people, and even more so the stability of the overall social order and the protection of public order and good customs. Since the implementation of the Amendment (VIII) to the Criminal Law of the PRC on May 1, 2011, the people's courts have handled a number of malicious wage arrears cases, effectively cracking down on criminals who evade payment of labor remuneration by transferring property, absconding, or other methods, or who have the ability to pay but refuse to pay labor remuneration, thereby creating a harmonious social atmosphere. In this case, the defendant Fu Dehong, in order to evade payment of labor remuneration, concealed his whereabouts, refused to pay a relatively large amount of labor remuneration, and failed to pay after being ordered by the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; his conduct constituted the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration. At the same time, a lighter punishment was imposed in consideration of Fu Dehong's admission of guilt after arrest, achieving proportionality between crime and punishment. The trial of this case clarified the elements of the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration, fully exerted the people's court's function of protecting people's livelihood, and provided strong support for the stability of the socialist market order.

III. Case of Revocation of Lin Li's Custody Rights

(1) Basic Facts

Lin Li (female), a villager of Wudian Village, Bangtou Town, Xianyou County, Fujian Province, repeatedly used a kitchen knife to cut the back and arms of her biological son Lin, who was only 9 years old, whipped Lin's legs with fire tongs, and often starved Lin. Starting from August 2013, cadres of Bangtou Town People's Government and Wudian Village Villagers' Committee, as well as police officers from Bangtou Police Station, repeatedly criticized and educated Lin Li, but Lin Li refused to reform. In January 2014, the Putian Municipal Communist Youth League Committee, the Municipal Women's Federation, together with Bangtou Town People's Government, Bangtou Police Station and other departments, jointly educated Lin Li. Lin Li wrote a written guarantee not to beat Lin again, but still did not show signs of remorse. In the early morning of May 29, Lin Li again used a kitchen knife to cut the back and arms of Lin. Consequently, Xianyou County Public Security Bureau imposed an administrative penalty on Lin Li of 15 days of administrative detention and a fine of RMB 1,000. The Putian Municipal Communist Youth League Committee, the Municipal Women's Federation and other relevant departments took emergency measures to send Lin to the municipal relief station for temporary placement. On June 13, the applicant Wudian Village Villagers' Committee, on the grounds that the respondent Lin Li had long abused Lin, seriously affecting Lin's physical and mental health, requested Xianyou County People's Court to revoke Lin Li's qualification as Lin's guardian and appoint Wudian Village Villagers' Committee as Lin's guardian. During the trial, Xianyou County People's Court solicited Lin's opinion. Lin expressed that he did not wish to live with his mother Lin Li and did not want to pursue Lin Li's criminal liability.

(2) Judgment

Xianyou County People's Court held after trial that a guardian should perform guardianship duties, protect the ward's physical health, care for the ward's life, and manage and educate the ward. The respondent Lin Li, as Lin's guardian, did not adopt correct methods to educate and guide Lin; because she thought Lin was disobedient, she used beating, scolding and other means to abuse Lin for a long time, and after being educated by relevant units still refused to reform, and again injured Lin with a kitchen knife; her conduct had seriously damaged Lin's physical and mental health, and she was therefore no longer suitable to serve as Lin's guardian. In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Law, the court ruled to revoke Lin Li's qualification as Lin's guardian and appointed the applicant Wudian Village Villagers' Committee as Lin's guardian.

(3) Significance

This case was the first case in Fujian Province involving the revocation of guardianship rights because a mother had long abused her minor child, and it is of great significance for the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of minors according to law.

Revoking parental guardianship is an important system for the state to protect the legitimate rights and interests of minors. Under normal circumstances, parents are the natural guardians of minor children, but if parents fail to perform guardianship duties, or even commit abuse, harm or other infringing acts against their children, allowing them to continue as guardians will seriously harm the child's growth. In such circumstances, in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Law, the Law on the Protection of Minors, and other laws, the minor child's grandparents, maternal grandparents, elder siblings, other close relatives and friends, as well as the unit where the minor's parents work, the village (neighborhood) committee in the minor's domicile, or the civil affairs department, all have the right to apply to the people's court to revoke the guardianship of the guardian who committed the infringing acts. In this case, the respondent Lin Li long abused her biological son Lin, who was only 9 years old, and after repeated dissuasion and education still refused to reform, seriously harming Lin's physical and mental health. Xianyou County People's Court, upon the application of the local villagers' committee, revoked Lin Li's guardianship qualification over Lin according to law. Because Lin's biological father was unknown and there were no other close relatives or friends who could serve as guardian, within the scope of persons who could serve as guardian as provided by law, and in accordance with the principle of best interests of the ward, Xianyou County People's Court appointed the local villagers' committee as Lin's guardian. After the judgment was announced, Xianyou County People's Court continued to track and follow up on Lin's placement. Considering that the villagers' committee indeed faced some specific difficulties in directly performing guardianship duties for Lin, the Putian Municipal Communist Youth League Committee, the Municipal Women's Federation, and the local civil affairs department actively researched and coordinated, and the civil affairs department arranged for alternative care for Lin, ensuring a safe, healthy, and happy growth environment for Lin.

Currently, cases of parents abusing minor children or infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of minor children still occur frequently. People's courts should implement the concept of "special and priority protection" for minors in their trial work, and protect the legitimate rights and interests of minors in accordance with the principle of maximizing the interests of minors. For guardians who have long infringed upon their minor children or seriously affected their physical and mental growth, their guardianship rights may be revoked according to law and another guardian appointed; for those with egregious circumstances or serious consequences, the guardian may also be held criminally liable for crimes such as abuse, abandonment, or intentional injury. In this case, if Lin or any other individual or unit with the right to file a complaint on his behalf brings a private criminal prosecution against Lin Li for the crime of abuse, the people's court should also accept it and make a criminal judgment according to law.

In protecting the legitimate rights and interests of minors, people's courts should fully exercise judicial initiative, pay attention to forming linkages with public security, civil affairs, Communist Youth League, women's federations, schools, hospitals, social work organizations, and other government agencies and social groups, to divide work and cooperate in making proper arrangements for the life, study, and psychological counseling of minors lacking parental care and family love, so that they can grow up safely and healthily. During the trial of this case, Xianyou County People's Court actively explored the trial of changing guardianship to protect the legitimate rights and interests of minors. The judge in charge of this case repeatedly visited Lin at the relief station and celebrated his birthday, allowing Lin to experience the humanistic care and warmth of the judiciary. After the judgment was announced, the judge also proactively communicated and coordinated with the municipal and county Communist Youth League Committees and Women's Federations to study and resolve issues regarding Lin's relief, placement, and schooling, creating good living and growth conditions for Lin. The trial of this case shows, on the one hand, that the people's court can indeed make a difference in serving the people through justice, and on the other hand, it also shows that protecting minors requires the common concern of the whole society and the cooperation and linkage of the government and various departments in order to achieve practical results.

IV. Tianjin Tianlong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. v. Jiangsu Xunong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Infringement of Plant New Variety Rights

(1) Basic Facts

The Northern Hybrid Japonica Rice Engineering Technology Center (same entity as Liaoning Rice Research Institute, operating under two names) and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute, Xuhuai Region, Jiangsu (hereinafter referred to as Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute) jointly developed the three-line hybrid japonica rice variety 9 You 418, which passed the national crop variety approval on November 10, 2000. The 9 You 418 rice variety originates from female parent 9201A and male parent C418. On December 30, 2003, Liaoning Rice Research Institute applied to the Ministry of Agriculture for a plant new variety right for the C418 rice variety, which was granted on May 1, 2007. On the same day, it licensed Tianjin Tianlong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianlong Company) to exclusively exploit the C418 plant new variety right.

On September 25, 2003, Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute applied to the Ministry of Agriculture for plant new variety right protection for its bred Xu 9201A rice variety, which was granted on January 1, 2007. On April 3, 2006, the Rice Office of Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute and Tianlong Company entered into an "Agreement on Introduction and Use of 'Xu 9201A'", stipulating: "Xu 9201A has applied for national variety right protection. In accordance with intellectual property protection requirements, introduction by external units is only permitted for test crossing and combination, not for commercial development, and it is guaranteed not to be disseminated to third parties; during use, without consent, it shall not be propagated on one's own, otherwise infringement liability will be pursued." On January 3, 2008, Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute licensed Jiangsu Xunong Seed Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xunong Company) to exclusively exploit the Xu 9201A plant new variety right.

The trial established that the combination used by Xunong Company and Tianlong Company to produce 9 You 418 was identical, both using male parent C418 and female parent Xu 9201A.

Tianlong Company and Xunong Company respectively filed lawsuits with the court, requesting confirmation that the other party had infringed upon their exclusive rights to the male parent C418 and female parent Xu 9201A plant new variety rights.

(2) Judgment

The cooperative breeding of 9 You 418 originated from the domestic hybrid rice research cooperation in the 1990s, which itself was a gratuitous combination. This variety has excellent traits and is widely planted in Jiangsu, Anhui, Henan, and other places; it is widely welcomed by growers and has become the leading variety of medium-japonica hybrid rice. 9 You 418 itself does not have a plant new variety right; the variety has entered the public domain. However, later Liaoning Rice Research Institute and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute respectively, through their own actions, indirectly obtained legal protection for the 9 You 418 variety. Liaoning Rice Research Institute applied for the plant new variety right for male parent C418 in 2003; that is, to produce 9 You 418 using male parent C418, authorization from the variety right holder, Liaoning Rice Research Institute, is required. Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute also applied for the plant new variety right for female parent Xu 9201A in 2003. Xunong Company admitted during litigation that it had sealed up all female parent 9201A that was not protected by variety rights, so Tianlong Company, as long as it produces 9 You 418, can only use female parent Xu 9201A. During the second instance, the court made extensive mediation efforts, hoping that both parties could grant each other licenses to allow the continued production of the excellent variety 9 You 418, but the parties ultimately failed to reach a compromise. Because Tianlong Company and Xunong Company could not reach a compromise, the 9 You 418 variety could not continue to be produced, which not only affected the interests of both parties but also actually harmed the national food production security and the public interest, and was inconsistent with the fundamental purpose of the original cooperative breeding between Liaoning Rice Research Institute and Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute, and also inconsistent with the fundamental requirement of promoting the transformation and implementation of new plant varieties. 9 You 418 is a three-line hybrid combination, integrating the excellent traits of both parents, with significant heterosis; the male parent and female parent have equal status and function in the combination of 9 You 418. Jiangsu High People's Court ruled that the cooperative parties of the 9 You 418 rice variety, Xuzhou Agricultural Science Research Institute and Liaoning Rice Research Institute, and their parties in this case, Xunong Company and Tianlong Company, all have the right to use the breeding materials of the parents for which the other party has obtained authorization, and shall waive the license fees mutally, but only for the production and sale of the 9 You 418 rice variety, and not for any other commercial purpose. Because Xunong Company had made considerable commercial efforts to promote the 9 You 418 variety and overcame cultivation technical difficulties, while Tianlong Company entered the production field only after the 9 You 418 variety had gained widespread market recognition, thereby significantly reducing the market cost of promoting the variety, to reflect fairness and reasonableness, the court also ordered Tianlong Company to pay Xunong Company RMB 500,000 as economic compensation. At the same time, because each party produced 9 You 418 on its own, there was indeed some degree of market competition and conflict of interest. The court warned both parties to comply with the relevant provisions of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC, operate honestly, compete in an orderly manner, ensure quality, and especially clearly mark their respective commercial logos to prevent new disputes and conflicts, and jointly maintain the good reputation of the 9 You 418 variety.

(3) Significance

Under normal circumstances, intellectual property rights are exclusive; without the permission of the right holder, others may not use the intellectual property arbitrarily. However, the essence of the intellectual property system is not just the protection of intellectual property, but more importantly, through protecting rights, to promote the use of intellectual property, realize its value, and drive technological development and economic and social progress. The dispute over the 9 You 418 hybrid rice variety in this case has a special historical background. 9 You 418 was bred through cooperation in the 1990s, with the parties providing the male parent and female parent respectively to jointly develop the variety. However, the subsequent production and exercise of intellectual property rights over the variety were not agreed upon by the cooperating parties, leading to the parties in this case, who respectively obtained exclusive exploitation licenses for the relevant male parent and female parent, accusing each other of infringement. After failing to mediate a mutual licensing agreement, Jiangsu High People's Court did not ultimately order both parties to cease infringement or prohibit either from using the other's protected plant new variety breeding materials. Instead, guided by legal principles, it broke conventional trial thinking, drew on the compulsory licensing system provided by intellectual property law, and on the basis of balancing the equal value of both the male and female parents to the production of the variety in question, directly ordered by judicial ruling that both parties grant each other licenses and waive license fees, thereby enabling the continued production of the widely promoted excellent hybrid rice variety 9 You 418. This judgment not only fundamentally served the common interests of both parties but also served the public interest of national food production security, and reflected the principle of fairness and the basic judicial value orientation of encouraging the transformation and implementation of new plant varieties. The trial idea of mutual licensing proposed in this case for the plant new variety right dispute was recognized by both parties and voluntarily performed, indicating that the legal and social effects of the judgment were good. The spirit of exploration and innovation reflected in this case also provides positive inspiration for judicially resolving similar intellectual property disputes.

V. Shandong Hongjitang Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. v. Shandong Hongjitang Ejiao Co., Ltd., et al. — Dispute over Trademark Infringement and Unfair Competition

(1) Basic Facts

"Hongjitang" is a time-honored brand of traditional Chinese medicine originating in Jinan, established in 1907. After multiple adjustments including splits, mergers, integrations, restructuring, and name changes, "Hongjitang" was divided into a pharmaceutical company and Shandong Hongjitang Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Pharmaceutical Group). The Ejiao Company in this case is a subsidiary established by the Pharmaceutical Group through investment. The Ejiao Company uses the "Hongjitang" trade name based on the investment relationship between the parent and subsidiary companies and has been lawfully registered and approved by the industry and commerce administration. The Pharmaceutical Company argued that the Ejiao Company prominently used "Hongjitang" on its ejiao products, along with the Ejiao Company's enterprise name and the words "Former Hongjitang Ejiao Factory," constituting trademark infringement and unfair competition. The Pharmaceutical Company requested the court to order the Ejiao Company to cease trademark infringement, stop using the "Hongjitang" trade name, and pay compensation for economic losses.

(II) Judgment

The Shandong High People's Court held, upon trial, that the Pharmaceutical Group and the Pharmaceutical Company had not historically formed a division of rights regarding the use of "Hongjitang." The Ejiao Company's use of the "Hongjitang" trade name was based on the historical inheritance and authorization of its parent company, the Pharmaceutical Group, and was not a malicious attempt to exploit the enterprise name or trademark of others. For conflicts of rights between trademarks and time-honored brands arising from historical reasons, the principles of good-faith coexistence and inclusive development should be applied in handling the matter. In this case, the Ejiao Company's use of the "Hongjitang" trademark and trade name was both historical and in good faith, and did not constitute trademark infringement or unfair competition. The court dismissed the Pharmaceutical Company's claims.

(III) Significance

This case provides typical guidance for handling disputes over rights in time-honored brands caused by historical reasons. The essence of conflicts over time-honored brand rights is how to determine the boundaries of rights and standardize use under market economy conditions for national traditional brands and time-honored brands with a century-long history after undergoing development under the planned economy system. Shandong courts, adhering to principles such as respect for history, protection of prior rights, good faith, and fair competition, lawfully handled the disputes between trademarks and time-honored brands, permitting the good-faith coexistence of the two "Hongjitang" trade names and achieving inclusive development among business operators.

VI. Wenzhou Rongsheng Trading Co., Ltd. v. Lucheng Branch of Wenzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce — Administrative Penalty Case

(I) Basic Facts

On March 16, 2011, the Lucheng Branch of the Administration for Industry and Commerce (Lucheng AIC) issued Administrative Penalty Decision No. (2011) 0137 against Rongsheng Company, finding that Rongsheng Company had distributed counterfeit "Guizhou Moutai" brand liquor, constituting an illegal act of infringing upon another's exclusive right to use a registered trademark. In accordance with the Trademark Law and relevant regulations, the defendant decided to impose the following penalties on the plaintiff's illegal acts: 1. Ordering the immediate cessation of the infringing acts; 2. Confiscating and destroying the 956 bottles of counterfeit "Guizhou Moutai" brand liquor that had been lawfully seized, and returning the remaining 129 bottles of "Guizhou Moutai" brand liquor and 109 cases of liquor; 3. Imposing a fine of RMB 500,000, to be turned over to the state treasury.

The Lucheng District People's Court of Zhejiang Province found upon trial: The "Guizhou Moutai" trademark was registered by Moutai Liquor Company and exclusively licensed to Kweichow Moutai Co., Ltd. On January 8, 2008, the defendant, Lucheng AIC, acting on a complaint from Moutai Liquor Company, inspected the business premises of the plaintiff, Rongsheng Company, and seized 1,085 bottles of "Guizhou Moutai" brand liquor suspected to be counterfeit, along with 109 cases of other liquor. Entrusted by the defendant, Kweichow Moutai Co., Ltd. conducted an appraisal of the involved "Guizhou Moutai" brand liquor on the following day, concluding that 956 bottles were counterfeit. Calculated at the plaintiff's listed prices, the total value of the 956 bottles of counterfeit "Guizhou Moutai" brand liquor was RMB 816,992. Due to the relatively large amount of counterfeit goods, on March 19, 2008, the defendant transferred the case to the Lucheng District Branch of the Wenzhou Public Security Bureau for handling. After investigation, the Lucheng District Branch of the Public Security Bureau failed to find evidence that the plaintiff knowingly sold counterfeit Moutai liquor and returned the case to the defendant on May 19, 2010. After holding a hearing and obtaining approval, the defendant issued the contested administrative penalty decision on March 16, 2011.

(II) Judgment

During the court hearing, both parties primarily engaged in cross-examination and argument regarding whether the authenticity appraisal forms issued by Moutai Company could be admitted as evidence. The Lucheng District People's Court of Zhejiang Province found upon trial that the goods sold by the plaintiff were appraised as counterfeit by the trademark registrant, and the plaintiff could not provide contrary evidence to rebut this. The defendant, therefore, accepted the appraisal conclusion and determined that the plaintiff had sold goods infringing upon another's exclusive right to use a registered trademark. The facts were clear and the evidence was sufficient. The plaintiff's illegal business turnover amounted to RMB 816,992. The defendant's contested administrative penalty was legally applicable. Accordingly, the court upheld the contested administrative penalty decision.

After the judgment was announced, Rongsheng Company refused to accept it and appealed.

The Wenzhou Intermediate People's Court found in the second instance that administrative evidence can only be used as the basis for deciding a case if it has been lawfully collected and verified by the administrative agency to confirm the facts of the case. Since the appraisal of trademark authenticity involves professional judgment unfamiliar to ordinary people, the accuracy of its conclusion is crucial to the parties concerned. Therefore, the appraiser should explain the basic circumstances such as the process of identification, the methods used, and the differences from genuine products, so that the administrative agency can judge and confirm the accuracy of the conclusion. However, the five appraisal forms issued by Kweichow Moutai Co., Ltd. simply recorded "Packaging materials: counterfeit; Liquor quality: not liquor produced by our company" and thus concluded "Counterfeit." The so-called appraisal content was too simplistic to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the conclusion, and the court did not admit it as evidence. The Lucheng AIC completely delegated the authority to determine the authenticity of the involved trademark to Moutai Company, solely on the grounds that Kweichow Moutai Co., Ltd. had the authority to appraise and could bear corresponding legal liability. The court did not support this. The administrative penalty decision made by Lucheng AIC against Rongsheng Company lacked sufficient primary evidence. Accordingly, the court reversed the original judgment, revoked the contested penalty decision, and ordered the Lucheng Branch of Wenzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce to re-handle the case within 60 days from the effective date of the judgment.

(III) Significance

Under China's current legal framework, the protection of intellectual property is divided into administrative and judicial channels. This case is a typical example of administrative disputes arising from administrative agencies investigating and punishing IP infringement. It was selected as one of the Top Ten Intellectual Property Cases in Zhejiang in 2011. The key issue in this case was the evidentiary review obligation of the administrative authority for industry and commerce in administrative cases of trademark infringement. The judiciary should both support administrative agencies in lawfully investigating and punishing IP infringement and fulfill its duty of judicial review over administrative agencies, properly resolving administrative disputes arising from IP enforcement through administrative litigation.

In recent years, with the development of the market economy, trademark registration applications have become increasingly active. The number of trademark infringement cases has risen continuously, and problems in administrative enforcement practices have become increasingly prominent. Since the appraisal of trademark authenticity involves professional knowledge and is difficult to judge, in the current practice of administrative enforcement against infringing trademarks, the administrative authorities for industry and commerce generally delegate the task of appraising trademark authenticity to the trademark registrant or lawful user, and use their written appraisal conclusions as evidence in administrative penalty cases. Once entering administrative litigation proceedings, administrative agencies often argue that the trademark registrant has the authority to appraise and bears the corresponding legal liability. This case is a typical example in this regard. Judicial practice has found that, due to the "authoritativeness" of their appraisal conclusions in administrative cases, the content of appraisal conclusions by trademark registrants or lawful users has become increasingly simplistic, sometimes failing to reflect the basic circumstances such as the identification process, methods used, and differences from genuine products, thereby undermining the accuracy and reliability of the conclusions. Strictly speaking, in terms of evidence classification, such appraisal conclusions are equivalent in nature to "victim statements" rather than expert conclusions under evidence law. Moreover, in many trademark penalty cases, the trademark registrant or lawful user is often also the complainant. If administrative agencies blindly abandon their review obligations and directly adopt these as conclusive evidence, it would not only violate the relevant provisions of evidence law but also contravene the principle of fairness. Therefore, before practices are fully unified, exploring the evidentiary review obligation of the administrative authorities for industry and commerce in trademark infringement cases has positive and practical significance.

VII. Qi Laifang v. Shandong Provincial Department of Transportation Road Transport Bureau — Failure to Perform Statutory Duties

(I) Basic Facts

On September 27, 2011, Qi Laifang entered into an agreement with Jinan Long-Distance Passenger Transport Co., Ltd. to contract bus number Lu A48307, operating on the route from Jinan to Jiaoyu. On November 9, 2012, Qi Laifang mailed an application to the Shandong Provincial Department of Transportation Road Transport Bureau, alleging that bus number Lu S30886 was operating beyond its designated route, encroaching upon his operating route, and requesting: lawfully investigate and punish the bus's unauthorized route operation; prohibit the bus from encroaching upon his route for operation; and revoke the road transport operation permit of the passenger transport operator. The bureau received the application but did not respond.

(II) Judgment

The Shizhong District People's Court of Jinan held in the first instance that, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Road Transport Regulations, where a passenger transport operator fails to operate according to the prescribed route, the road transport management agency at or above the county level shall investigate and punish such conduct; where the circumstances are serious, the original permitting authority shall revoke the road transport operation permit. In this case, the Shandong Provincial Department of Transportation Road Transport Bureau was the issuing authority for the road transport operation permit of bus Lu S30886. If Qi Laifang believed that the bus was not operating according to the prescribed route, he should have filed a complaint with the county-level road transport management agency. Only if the county-level road transport management agency determined that the circumstances were serious would the matter be transferred to the Shandong Provincial Department of Transportation Road Transport Bureau for handling. Qi Laifang's self-determination that the violation by bus Lu S30886 was serious and his request for the provincial-level road transport authority to handle the matter did not comply with the above jurisdictional provisions, and the claim should be dismissed.

The Jinan Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance that the "Shandong Province Road Transport Regulations" and other provisions clearly authorize the provincial-level traffic inspection authorities to investigate and punish passenger transport operators who fail to operate according to the prescribed route. Although the Shandong Provincial Department of Transportation Road Transport Bureau was the issuing authority for the road passenger transport line operation permit of bus Lu S30886, it did not have the enforcement authority to conduct roadside inspections to determine whether the bus was operating outside the prescribed route. Only when a passenger transport operator has engaged in unauthorized route operation and the circumstances are serious does the bureau have the power to revoke the road transport operation permit. However, given that the above provision is a special provision under the Administrative Licensing Law concerning the duty of the licensing authority to supervise and inspect the activities of the licensee under the permitted scope, upon receiving the application, the bureau should provide appropriate guidance in accordance with its scope of authority. The court reversed the original judgment and ordered the Shandong Provincial Department of Transportation Road Transport Bureau to handle Qi Laifang's application within 60 days from the receipt of the judgment, in accordance with the scope of its authority.

(III) Significance

Promoting openness in administrative procedures and ensuring the open, efficient, and convenient exercise of power is a historical task entrusted to the courts by the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China. Compelling administrative agencies to fulfill their obligation of clarification and provide appropriate guidance to citizens, legal persons, or other organizations on matters they apply for, even if those matters are not within the scope of the agency's functions, is an important lever for courts to promote openness in administrative procedures and facilitate the efficient and convenient exercise of power. However, currently, judicial review of administrative agencies remains at the level of requiring compliance with statutory duties, with insufficient attention to the obligation of clarification. This case highlights the administrative agency's obligation of clarification, clarifying that when an applicant requests the agency to perform its duties under general laws, the agency cannot ignore the request on the grounds that special laws have different provisions. Instead, it should provide necessary explanations and guidance, thereby effectively promoting the open, efficient, and convenient exercise of administrative power.

VIII. Liu Zirong v. Miquan City Bureau of Labor and Social Security — Work-Related Injury Determination Case

(I) Basic Facts

On January 7, 2001, Liu Zirong, the deputy mine manager of the No. 3 Mine of Tiegou Town, Miquan City, Xinjiang, learned that the top of the coal seam storage bin was empty, which would pose a safety hazard to coal mine production. At approximately 10 p.m. on January 8, Liu Zirong and blaster Yu Yuangui were together in the staff dormitory modifying instantaneous detonators into delayed-action detonators when the detonators exploded, blowing off Liu Zirong's left thumb, index finger, and middle finger, and injuring his ring finger. After the incident, the Tiegou Town Coal Mine immediately sent Liu Zirong to the hospital for treatment and covered all his medical expenses. On March 21, the Tiegou Town Coal Mine and Liu Zirong reached a compensation agreement, under which the coal mine paid Liu Zirong a one-time subsidy of RMB 15,000 for his future living expenses and nutrition expenses. On April 9, Liu Zirong applied to the Miquan City Labor Bureau for a work-related injury determination. On July 3, 2002, the Miquan City Labor Bureau issued a "Decision on Not Determining Liu Zirong's Injury as Work-Related" (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision").

(II) Judgment

The Miquan City People's Court, in the first instance, held that the Miquan City Labor Bureau had incorrectly applied laws and regulations and therefore reversed the "Decision" of the Miquan City Labor Bureau.

The Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court, in the second instance, held that the determination decision made by the Miquan City Labor Bureau on Liu Zirong's work-related injury application was based on clear facts, correctly applied the law, and followed lawful procedures. The court reversed the administrative judgment of the Miquan City People's Court in the first instance and upheld the "Decision" of the Miquan City Labor Bureau.

The High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, upon retrial, upheld the administrative judgment of the second instance.

The Supreme People's Court, upon exercising its power of adjudication supervision, held that in accordance with the "Trial Measures for Work-Related Injury Insurance of Enterprise Employees," injuries, disabilities, or deaths occurring while an employee is engaged in the daily production or work of the unit, or in temporary work assigned by the unit's responsible person, or in emergency situations where, though not assigned by the unit's responsible person, the employee is engaged in work directly related to the major interests of the unit, shall be determined as work-related injuries. Liu Zirong, as the deputy mine manager of the No. 3 Mine of Tiegou Town, Miquan City, modified instantaneous detonators into delayed-action detonators with another blaster in the worker dormitory based on the normal production needs of the mine, and was injured in the detonator explosion. This conduct was clearly directly related to the work needs and interests of the unit. The Ministry of Public Security's "Opinion on How to Characterize the Act of Modifying Instantaneous Detonators into Delayed-Action Detonators" stated that detonators contain hazardous substances such as high explosives and primary explosives, and modifying instantaneous detonators into delayed-action detonators without any protective measures constitutes a serious violation of national safety regulations and quality and technical performance requirements for civil explosive products, and should not be characterized as the illegal manufacture of explosive materials. Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court reversed the administrative judgment of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; reversed the administrative judgment of the Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture Intermediate People's Court; upheld the administrative judgment of the Miquan City People's Court; and ordered the Midong District Bureau of Human Resources and Social Security of Urumqi, Xinjiang, to make a new specific administrative act within two months from the date of receipt of the judgment.

(III) Significance

How to accurately grasp the criteria for determining work-related injuries has always been a difficult issue in administrative litigation cases concerning work-related injury determinations. This case involves difficult issues in work-related injury determinations, such as how to understand the circumstances where an injury shall not be deemed work-related and how to define the "major interests of the unit." The Supreme People's Court's judgment, starting from the legislative purpose of protecting the vital interests of employees, adopted a strict approach to circumstances where injuries shall not be deemed work-related. It clarified that if an employee is injured while engaging in dangerous work outside the workplace due to the needs of the unit's work, even if there is some regulatory violation, the work should still be considered directly related to the major interests of the unit, and thus the injury shall be determined as work-related. This judgment fully reflects the legislative intent of work-related injury insurance and has important demonstrative significance for grasping and unifying the standards for adjudicating administrative cases involving work-related injury determinations.
